comparison: Both evaluate heterologous expression experiments in C. elegans (C89-C94). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with caveats about experimental conditions, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 expressing confusion about the feeding rescue experiment and requesting additional localized expression data.

Both evaluate developmental effects of ZTDO. OpenEval finds extensive support for claims C2-C5, C27-C39 about concentration-dependent and stage-specific effects. Peer reviewers also find these claims SUPPORTED (C2-C5, C27-C39, C40-C45), explicitly praising findings as 'interesting' and 'unexpected and exciting' with no concerns raised.

Both evaluate dauer exit inhibition data. OpenEval finds claims C40-C45 SUPPORTED by Figure 2G data showing species specificity and genetic epistasis. Peer reviewers also find these claims SUPPORTED as part of the 'interesting' developmental effects, with no specific concerns raised.

Both evaluate chemosensory specificity. OpenEval finds claims C21, C23-C26 SUPPORTED by chemotaxis assays and complementation analysis. Peer reviewers find C23-C26 SUPPORTED, accepting the specificity findings, though Reviewer 1 noted a data presentation issue between figures.

Partial overlap on C21 (genetic complementation). OpenEval finds C21 SUPPORTED as part of chemosensory phenotype characterization. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 explicitly requesting additional data to support the claim that tu404 and tu405 are allelic and questioning whether they might not be allelic.

Partial overlap on C48-C49 (sequencing data). OpenEval finds molecular cloning and sequencing data (C46-C55) SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN for C48-C49, questioning whether tu404 and tu405 are truly allelic and noting only tu404 was molecularly characterized.

Both evaluate transgenic rescue experiments. OpenEval finds claims C46-C55 SUPPORTED, including rescue of all three phenotypes (C52-C54). Peer reviewers find C52-C55 SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 3 stating 'The cloning is quite convincing, with transgenic rescue' and describing work as 'rigorous and clearly presented.'

Both evaluate morphological phenotype data (C46-C47). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED as part of comprehensive molecular characterization. Peer reviewers also find C46-C47 SUPPORTED, accepting the morphological phenotype used for positional mapping without question.

Both evaluate transcript abundance data (C50-C51). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED as part of molecular characterization. Peer reviewers also find C50-C51 SUPPORTED, though Reviewer 1 questioned use of 'Interestingly' and requested notation about how equal abundance was determined.

Both evaluate sequence analysis and phylogenetic findings (C56-C59). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by computational analysis, with caveat about branch length interpretation for C59. Peer reviewers also find C56-C59 SUPPORTED, accepting bioinformatic analyses without critique.

Minimal overlap on C6 (protein domain predictions). OpenEval finds C6 SUPPORTED as part of computational sequence analysis. Peer reviewers find gene identification and rescue (C6, C7, C52-C55) SUPPORTED, praising the cloning as 'quite convincing.'

Both evaluate P. pacificus expression pattern data (C69-C71, C74-C76, C80). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by transgenic reporter analysis with reasonable cell identification. Peer reviewers also find these claims SUPPORTED, accepting the P. pacificus expression data without question, though concerns were raised about C. elegans methodology.

Minimal overlap on C7 (expression pattern). OpenEval finds C7 SUPPORTED as part of detailed expression analysis. Peer reviewers find related rescue and cloning data (C6, C7, C52-C55) SUPPORTED, with no concerns about the expression pattern itself.

Both evaluate C. elegans expression pattern and species comparison (C84-C88). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with caveat that C88 could benefit from functional validation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 raising major concern that transgenic reporter alone is insufficient and requesting smFISH to establish convincing negative expression result.

Both evaluate sequence similarity and behavioral differences (C82-C83). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED, noting expression pattern differences provide plausible explanation. Peer reviewers also find C82-C83 SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 accepting the observation while suggesting protein function differences could contribute.

Both evaluate C. elegans body morphology phenotype (C66-C68). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by RNAi and mutant analysis showing conserved role. Peer reviewers also find C66-C68 SUPPORTED, accepting the body morphology data without concerns.

Both evaluate C. elegans missense mutant and chemosensory phenotype (C63-C64). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with caveat that missense may not fully disrupt function. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 stating it's unclear what effect the D48N mutation has and requesting RNAi experiments instead.

OpenEval evaluated ecological and evolutionary interpretations (C8, C96-C100, C105-C109, C112, C114-C118) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative hypotheses lacking direct experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these interpretive claims.

OpenEval evaluated background claims and citations (C9-C20, C60-C62, C65, C72, C77, C95, C101-C104, C110-C111, C113) as SUPPORTED, noting these provide context from previous work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval evaluated general biodiversity statements (C1, C13) as SUPPORTED established scientific knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these general knowledge claims.
